thread:
Emma: @Kevin FYI — ACME reported a surprise invoice bump (~+12k tokens) for a handful of sessions on 2026-03-05. They say the client closed the socket mid-response. Our billing ledger shows those sessions as full completions. Can we triage?
Kevin: Can you paste one session id + timeframe? also link to their dashboard snapshot if you have it.
Emma: Session id sess_8a7f2e3 timeframe ~2026-03-05T14:22Z. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/customers/acme/sessions?sess=sess_8a7f2e3 — they attached app logs showing client cancel right after first chunk.
Lisa: Ack. I see repeated pattern across 6 sessions that day, all same client library version (acme-client v1.4.2).
Raj: Quick hypothesis: when the client TCP closes mid-SSE, the runtime emits a STREAM_END event but the metering agent sometimes replays the "final_frame" accounting path on retry, double-adding tokens. We have a few related flags in the router. Need logs from runtime and metering component.
Emma: I pulled runtime trace and the metering log for sess_8a7f2e3:
```
[runtime] 2026-03-05T14:22:03.112Z sess=sess_8a7f2e3 chunk: tokens=84 prefix=hello
[client] connection reset by peer
[runtime] 2026-03-05T14:22:03.118Z sess=sess_8a7f2e3 stream_closed reason=client_disconnect
[metering] 2026-03-05T14:22:03.119Z sess=sess_8a7f2e3 streamed_tokens=84
[metering] 2026-03-05T14:22:03.121Z sess=sess_8a7f2e3 finalize_path invoked final_tokens=172
[billing] 2026-03-05T14:22:03.125Z sess=sess_8a7f2e3 ledger_increment=172
```
Raj: That finalize_path call is unexpected given the immediate client_disconnect. Looks like the metering agent received both the streamed prefix and a late finalize RPC (from router or a retry path).
Kevin: If ledger_increment used final_tokens we billed 172 but only 84 reached the client — customer rightly upset.
Lisa: Repro plan I can try quickly: use curl to open SSE, read first "data:" chunk then close TCP immediately. See if billing records both streamed and finalized. Example: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d '{"model":"x","prompt":"..."}'` then ctrl-c after first chunk.
Raj: I'll instrument a local dev build to log the metering rpc that triggers finalize. If we confirm duplicated accounting, patch is probably a dedupe guard in the metering service keyed by (session_id, finalize_token_reported).
Emma: Customer wants interim credit while we investigate. Kevin, can billing create a provisional credit for the 6 affected sessions? Suggest full refund of the delta (final - streamed).
Kevin: I'll open PLAT-5879 and credit ACME for delta > 100 tokens per session. Creating ticket now.
Emma: PLAT-5879 created. CC: @billing-bot for audit trail.
billing-bot: [automated] Ticket PLAT-5879 created by Kevin. Action: provisional credit queued, awaiting engineering confirmation.
Raj: Quick note for repro: I found an alternate route where router retried the request to another worker after socket close; the retry completed and triggered finalize RPC while streamed_tokens already recorded. So dedupe must survive cross-worker retries.
Lisa: That matches customer app: they showed a single session id but multiple worker ids in runtime trace.
Raj: Action items: 1) I will add a cross-worker finalize dedupe (idempotency key = session_id + finalize_nonce) and add a 200ms debounce on finalize RPCs. 2) Add a short-lived dashboard column to surface streamed_tokens vs billed_tokens per session. 3) Add an e2e test that force-closes client between chunks.
Kevin: Once Raj confirms a fix branch, I'll approve credits and notify ACME support rep.
Emma: Thanks all. I'll reply to customer with repro steps and tell them we have a ticket (PLAT-5879) and are provisioning a credit while we fix.
Raj: I'll post PR link and rough ETA in this thread when ready.
Lisa: Repro notes for internal doc: customer used long-poll SSE, client lib closed connection on memory spike — reproducible locally. Use `abrupt-close` test script: https://ci.redwood.internal/tests/abrupt-close (dev only).
Emma: closing loop — next update by EOW or earlier if fix lands. :thumbsup:
